source_text: Impudenter igitur sub umbra eius nominis delitescis, cum nimis diversa contrariaque dicatis. Ille enim arguit opus hominum, tu opus Dei; ille studia delinquentium, tu innocentiam vitamque nascentium; ille voluntatem hominum, tu naturam.
pass_a_gloss: You therefore hide shamelessly under the shadow of his name, when you say things too diverse and contrary. For he accuses the work of human beings, you the work of God; he the pursuits of those offending, you the innocence and life of those being born; he the will of human beings, you nature.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: You therefore hide shamelessly in the shadow of his name, although your statements are greatly different and opposed. He accuses human beings’ work; you accuse God’s work. He accuses sinners’ deliberate conduct; you accuse newborn children’s innocence and life. He accuses human will; you accuse nature.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
